newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir suffers setback in oxygen system repairs.
newsitem.headline: Mir suffers setback in oxygen system repairs.

text.p: The accident-prone crew aboard Mir, expecting a relief crew in just hours, realised on Thursday they could not immediately mend the space station's oxygen supply system -- the latest problem to develop on the ailing craft.
"We have encountered new problems with the Elektron system," deputy flight director Viktor Blagov told Reuters.

The crew have concluded they must replace rather than repair blocked piping leading to the Elektron, so they must wait for the U.S. space shuttle Atlantis, due to dock with Mir in late September, to bring new piping, he said.
The Elektron system has not worked since last week despite the crew's continued repair efforts.

The delay means the new crew of arriving commander Anatoly Solovyov, 49, and engineer Pavel Vinogradov, 43, who are due to dock with Mir at 1703 GMT, would face yet another repair headache on their mission, which will determine the future of the ailing space station.

Until the newer Elektron system is restored, cosmonauts will try to revive the older, back-up Elektron in the Kvant-2 module, which was powered down to save energy after Mir collided with a resupply ship on June 25, causing a major loss of energy.

"They will try to crank up the back-up Elektron, which is in working condition but is simply not connected to the power supply," Blagov said. "All they need is a spare cable to plug it in. We hope we will manage to find it on Mir."
Until then, cosmonauts will relying on a more than two-month supply of oxygen candles, officials said.
The crew are hoping to forget their woes at least for a while on Thursday when they open the hatch to welcome the relief cosmonauts on board at about 1830 GMT.
"They'll meet in the base block and there will be, we can say, a holiday spirit, " Mission Control spokesman Valery Lyndin said.
Solovyov and Vinogradov were expected to add to the festive mood with fresh food and souvenirs from Earth, he said.

The two crews will share the quarters on Mir, a collection of different modules, until August 14, when current commander Vasily Tsibliyev and engineer Alexander Lazutkin, who have been in orbit since February, return to Earth.
British-American physicist Michael Foale will remain on board until late September when NASA astronaut David Wolf, who is now in training outside Moscow, is scheduled to replace him.
The festive atmosphere of welcoming the new crew is unlikely to last for long as they must quickly gear up for major repairs.

Vinogradov will lead risky efforts to restore power on Mir by opening the hatch to the airless, darkened Spektr module on August 20 and reconnecting cables that lead to solar panels outside. Success in the operation will restore much of Mir's energy supply.
Vinogradov is arriving on Mir for the first time. Solovyov, one of Russia's most experienced cosmonauts, has flown four times on Mir for a total of 456 days in space.
